title: Reading the table
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The uncle reads the tide table aloud the way other men read weather. Gully repeats it back with his eyes closed. Gets Thursday wrong. The uncle says Thursday's the one that matters. He doesn't say why.

panels.composition: The shack. The UNCLE with the tide table, reading. GULLY, eyes closed, repeating. WOOD and BARNABY.

balloons.text: Wednesday, minus one point two, six-forty.

image.prompt: an old man reading from a tide table inside a bait shack while a teenager with eyes closed repeats after him, a young man and a dog listening, black and white, no words

balloons.text: Thursday, minus one point four, seven-twenty.

image.prompt: a stocky teenager with his eyes closed reciting, black and white, no words
an old weathered man folding a tide table, flat, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood drawing the two of them. He's written the numbers in the margin of the drawing. Thursday's underlined. He doesn't know why either.

image.prompt: a young man drawing two figures with tide numbers noted in the margin of his pad, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: 'Learn it and you'll know.' Thursday, underlined, reserved.
